title: Beyond the 956: Bob Boone, Phillies World Series champion catcher, dies at 78
excerpt: Bob Boone, the four-time All-Star catcher who backstopped the Philadelphia Phillies to their first World Series championship in 1980, has died at 78. He died Monday, November 9, 2026, his son Bret Boone confirmed.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Bob Boone, the four-time All-Star catcher who backstopped the Philadelphia Phillies to their first World Series championship in 1980, has died at 78.

Boone died on Monday, November 9, 2026. His son, former All-Star second baseman Bret Boone, confirmed the news in a social media post late Monday.

Born Robert Raymond Boone on November 19, 1947, in San Diego, Boone was drafted by the Phillies out of Stanford University in 1969 and reached the majors in 1972. Over 19 seasons with the Phillies (1972–1981), the California Angels (1982–1988) and the Kansas City Royals (1989–1990), he played 2,225 games at catcher — the third-most in major league history — batting .254 with 105 home runs and 826 RBIs.

Boone was a four-time All-Star and won seven Gold Glove Awards. He was behind the plate for the Phillies' 1980 World Series win over the Kansas City Royals, the franchise's first championship, and was inducted into the Phillies Wall of Fame in 2005.

After his playing career, Boone managed the Kansas City Royals from 1995 to 1997 and the Cincinnati Reds from 2001 to 2003.

Boone was the middle link in baseball's first three-generation major league family. His father, Ray Boone, was a two-time All-Star infielder. His sons Bret and Aaron both played in the majors; Aaron Boone is the manager of the New York Yankees.

Rest in Peace, Bob Boone.

Sources: New York Post; Sports Illustrated; PhillyVoice.
